scope: Current production Rust/Python is unchanged from the 693-test provisional-hold repair. This turn adds a native execution probe and finite workflow composition model; no new runtime defect was observed in these executions.

large.scope: One native successful raw publication, one incomplete record_set with its established hold, source staging release, four disjoint authenticated range readers, original handoff retry, explicit close of another failed preparation, lost consume response, peer GC and fresh post-GC consume retry. Random 8 MiB pattern repeated. Pattern/chunk-metadata construction excluded from publication timing; payload hash/framing/fsync included. Reader output range <=256 MiB plus bounded authentication scratch. Reader aggregate includes SSH startup, chunks are correlated and hosts share the file; no cache eviction or independent p99/SLA/physical-backend bandwidth inference. No Python/FFI or actual TB transfer claim.

cpu_observation.scope: Cumulative Linux process CPU counters, starting monitoring late in publication. The first ready sample includes pattern preparation and control work as well as publication; it is not exact per-API CPU time. Last sample precedes exit. No filesystem/device bottleneck attribution follows.

measured_parameters.file_nodes_scope: One source payload file plus one 1152-byte completed manifest; failed output is removed before this phase. Actual 100 GB bytes are abstracted into the payload node.

model.reader_outcome: Success-only configurations finish; failures-allowed configuration ends done or protected failed. Failed-reader cleanup is an unsafe candidate, not the current supervisor behavior. Native 100 GB run does not inject reader failures.
model.timing_scope: 373 real disjoint chunks; 372 full 256 MiB chunks determine nearest-rank quantiles. They are correlated within one file/run, not independent whole-file publication/read samples, and no measured delay or bandwidth enters liveness premises.

unchanged_production_evidence_reused.manifest_change: Cargo.toml adds only workflow_extent_probe example; no production sources, dependencies or features change.
unchanged_production_evidence_reused.reuse_scope: Exact Verus inputs and consumer list unchanged. Existing environment statements/review/source contracts unchanged; registry only adds a TLA consumer and evidence links. Original proof registry remains archived without rewriting its hash. New native probe itself is executed/clippy-checked, not Verus-proved.

attempt_history: Initial example Clippy rejected a manual multiple-of test; the probe uses is_multiple_of and was rebuilt before both measurements.

Initial focused workflow model checked only successful reader completion. It was replaced before the full run with explicit success/error outcomes: failed readers preserve ownership and terminate safely rather than being assumed to succeed. Both focused reports are retained.
unproved: Real I/O/network termination, filesystem/lock/catalog refinement and whole Store/Rust binary correctness
Arbitrary multi-file graphs, physical crashes, process-restart cleanup and reader-failure recovery
Long-run sustained bandwidth, cold-cache or physical backend rates, independent p99 and workload-wide performance SLA
Actual TB transfers: this run is capped at 100 decimal GB; earlier sparse TB offset tests remain separate
